content: 1. For individuals with comorbidities, it is recommended to use the lowest effective doses of medications that are associated with weight gain to minimize adverse effects. 2. In patients with type 2 diabetes, preference should be given to glucose-lowering medications that are either weight-neutral or promote weight loss. 3. Pharmacological treatment for obesity is advised for individuals with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher, or for those with a BMI of 27 or higher who have weight-related complications, particularly when lifestyle modifications alone are insufficient. 4. When prescribing pharmacotherapy for obesity, GLP-1 receptor agonists and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists are the preferred options due to their proven efficacy in achieving significant weight reduction. 5. To optimize the effectiveness of weight management medications, they should be combined with structured lifestyle changes and behavioral therapy interventions.
